\section{Research Experience}

\begin{cventries}
  \roleentry{Calculus of Variations --- Variable-Coefficient Differential Constraints}
            {Spring 2026 -- present}
            {Carnegie Mellon University.\factsep Research advisor:
             \href{https://irenefonseca.weebly.com}{Irene Fonseca}.}
\begin{cvbullets}
  \item Study weak lower semicontinuity under variable-coefficient linear constraints
    and its characterization by frozen $\A$-quasiconvexity, beyond Santos's setting of
    smooth coefficients with uniform constant rank.
  \item Proved sufficiency for Lipschitz coefficients with pointwise constant rank, so
    the rank may vary in space, using blow-up and frozen-operator projections.
  \item Proved necessity wherever, for each lattice direction, the rank of the symbol is
    locally constant, by adapting the Davoli--Fonseca moving-kernel construction instead
    of pseudodifferential calculus.
\end{cvbullets}

  \roleentry{M.S.\ Thesis --- Nonlinear Elliptic PDE and Stochastic Games}
            {Fall 2025 -- present}
            {University of Pittsburgh.\factsep Advisor:
             \href{https://sites.pitt.edu/~manfredi/}{Juan J.\ Manfredi}.}
  \begin{cvbullets}
    \item Identified the regularized $p$-Laplacian with the ordinary
          $p$-Laplacian of an affine lift one dimension higher, and computed
          the projected noise kernel and tilted extremal terms.
    \item Established existence, uniqueness, and Borel measurability for
          the projected dynamic programming principle with strip boundary
          data, using monotone iteration and a comparison principle
          adapted to the tilted terms.
    \item Identified the unique solution with the value of an explicit
          projected tug-of-war game on an augmented state space, using
          super/submartingale arguments and measurable almost-optimal
          strategies.
    \item Proved convergence to the viscosity solution as $\varepsilon\to 0$
          for $p\ge 2$ and a pointwise asymptotic mean value characterization
          for $C^2$ solutions throughout $1<p<\infty$; constructed a
          counterexample at the formal endpoint $p=\infty$.
  \end{cvbullets}
\end{cventries}
